initiatives.name: Ongoing Service Evidence Programmes
initiatives.summary: SJP made good progress with its historic ongoing service evidence review programme, releasing £109.5 million from the associated provision during 2025. The company remains confident the exercise will complete in 2026.

evidence.title: Historic Ongoing Service Evidence Review Programme
evidence.summary: SJP continued its review of historic client servicing records announced in February 2024, involving clients charged for ongoing advice services since 2018 where evidence falls below acceptable standards. The Group developed processes to make repayments where evidence is inadequate and released £109.5 million from provisions.
evidence.quote: In February 2024 SJP announced a review of historic client servicing records. This has involved actively reviewing records of a sub-population of clients that has been charged for ongoing advice services since the start of 2018 but where the evidence of delivery of the ongoing advice service falls below an acceptable standard. The Group has continued to develop processes and controls to enable it to make repayments to clients where the evidence of delivery falls below the acceptable standard.

evidence.title: Ongoing Service Evidence Programme
evidence.summary: SJP made good progress with its historic ongoing service evidence review programme, releasing £109.5 million from the associated provision during 2025. The company remains confident the exercise will complete in 2026.
evidence.quote: During 2025 we also made good progress with our OSE programme, which has resulted in two releases from the associated provision - full details are set out in the CFO's report. With the business deep into the operational phase of this complex project, we remain confident that we will complete the exercise in 2026.

initiatives.name: Simple Comparable Charging Structure Implementation
initiatives.summary: SJP successfully implemented a new simple, comparable charging structure in August 2025 after almost two years of development. This fundamental change makes it easier for clients to understand charges and assess value across SJP's holistic proposition.

evidence.title: Simple Comparable Charging Structure Implementation
evidence.summary: SJP successfully implemented a new simple, comparable charging structure in August 2025 after almost two years of development. This fundamental change makes it easier for clients to understand charges and assess value across SJP's holistic proposition.
evidence.quote: Our simple, comparable charging structure went live from 26 August 2025. This was a significant change that was carefully planned and successfully executed.

initiatives.name: Group Risk Committee Leadership Transition
initiatives.summary: Penny James was appointed as Chair of the Group Risk Committee in December 2025, replacing Rosemary Hilary who retired from the Board. The Committee also saw other membership changes with new appointments and departures during the year.

evidence.title: New Group Risk Committee Chair Appointed
evidence.summary: Penny James was appointed as Chair of the Group Risk Committee in December 2025, replacing Rosemary Hilary who retired from the Board. The Committee also saw other membership changes with new appointments and departures during the year.
evidence.quote: Following my appointment as Chair of the Committee in December 2025, I am pleased to present my first report to you on the Committee's activities in the year. I would like to extend thanks to Rosemary Hilary for her strong leadership of the Committee during her tenure.

initiatives.name: Shareholder Returns and Capital Allocation
initiatives.summary: SJP completed multiple share buy-back programmes during 2025, including an interim programme of £95.5 million and announced final programmes totalling £218.1 million for 2025. This represents a significant capital return to shareholders following their revised distribution approach.

evidence.title: Increased Shareholder Returns Policy
evidence.summary: SJP updated its shareholder returns guidance a year earlier than planned, increasing the payout ratio from 50% to 70% of the Underlying cash result for 2026 and beyond. This comprises an ordinary dividend of at least 28% and share buy-backs for the balance.
evidence.quote: For the 2026 financial year and beyond, the Board intends to return 70% of the Underlying cash result to shareholders. This will comprise: an ordinary dividend, which we expect will make up at least 40% of total shareholder returns. This is equivalent to at least 28% of the Underlying cash result; and a share buy-back for the balance.

evidence.title: Share Buy-back Programmes Totalling £218.1 Million
evidence.summary: SJP completed multiple share buy-back programmes during 2025, including an interim programme of £95.5 million and announced final programmes totalling £218.1 million for 2025. This represents a significant capital return to shareholders following their revised distribution approach.
evidence.quote: Under the authority granted by shareholders at the 2025 AGM, the Directors have resolved to undertake a final share buy-back programme with respect to 2025, committing to purchase shares up to a maximum value of £103.9 million. An additional share buy-back programme, to return capital to shareholders following a release of the Ongoing Service Evidence provision, will be undertaken, committing to purchase shares up to a maximum value of £18.7 million... Together, this will bring the total share buy-back in respect to 2025 to a maximum value of £218.1 million.

initiatives.name: Polaris Multi-Index Fund Range Launch
initiatives.summary: SJP launched the Polaris Multi-Index range of lower-cost multi-asset funds in October 2025, complementing existing solutions and enhancing choice for clients across risk profiles. The new fund range grew to over £1 billion in funds under management by year-end.

evidence.title: Polaris Multi-Index Fund Range Launch
evidence.summary: SJP launched the Polaris Multi-Index range of lower-cost multi-asset funds in October 2025, complementing existing solutions and enhancing choice for clients across risk profiles. The new fund range grew to over £1 billion in funds under management by year-end.
evidence.quote: We capitalised on our new charging structure being in place by launching the Polaris Multi-Index range of funds in October. This range of lower-cost multi-asset funds of funds implements our active asset allocation expertise through index-tracking funds. FUM in Polaris Multi-Index surpassed the £1 billion mark by the end of the year, only two months after launch.

initiatives.name: SJP Charitable Foundation Donation
initiatives.summary: SJP donated £500,000 of unclaimed dividends to the SJP Charitable Foundation in 2025, with funding primarily focused on supporting disadvantaged individuals and communities with their financial wellbeing over the next three years. This reflects their commitment to financial education and societal impact.

evidence.title: £500,000 Donation to SJP Charitable Foundation
evidence.summary: SJP donated £500,000 of unclaimed dividends to the SJP Charitable Foundation in 2025, with funding primarily focused on supporting disadvantaged individuals and communities with their financial wellbeing over the next three years. This reflects their commitment to financial education and societal impact.
evidence.quote: In 2025, we were delighted to donate £500,000 of unclaimed dividends to the SJP Charitable Foundation. This funding will primarily focus on supporting disadvantaged individuals and communities with their financial wellbeing over the next three years.

initiatives.name: Board Refreshment with New Directors
initiatives.summary: SJP appointed Helen Beck and Penny James to the Board during 2025, succeeding chairs of the Group Remuneration and Risk Committees respectively. Evelyn Bourke will join the Board in March 2026, while Rosemary Hilary retired at end of 2025.

evidence.title: Board Refreshment with New Directors
evidence.summary: SJP appointed Helen Beck and Penny James to the Board during 2025, succeeding chairs of the Group Remuneration and Risk Committees respectively. Evelyn Bourke will join the Board in March 2026, while Rosemary Hilary retired at end of 2025.
evidence.quote: Helen Beck and Penny James joined the Board during 2025, succeeding the chairs of the Group Remuneration and Risk Committees respectively. Both have brought experience and diverse perspectives to the Board, gained during their extensive executive and non-executive careers. Rosemary Hilary retired from the Board at the end of 2025, and I would like to express the Board's gratitude for her important contribution over the last few years. I am delighted to also welcome Evelyn Bourke, who will be joining the Board on 1 March 2026.

initiatives.name: Cost and Efficiency Programme
initiatives.summary: SJP is implementing a multi-year programme to reshape its cost base and remove around £100 million per annum from addressable costs by 2027. The company completed a new organisational design, reduced property footprint, and optimized commercial relationships with suppliers.

evidence.title: Cost and Efficiency Programme
evidence.summary: SJP is implementing a multi-year programme to reshape its cost base and remove around £100 million per annum from addressable costs by 2027. The company completed a new organisational design, reduced property footprint, and optimized commercial relationships with suppliers.
evidence.quote: We progressed our multi-year programme to reshape our cost base for the future and remain on track to remove around £100 million from addressable costs by 2027. During 2025, we completed the implementation of a new organisational design, reduced our property footprint and began optimising our commercial relationships with suppliers.

initiatives.name: Cyber Security and Operational Resilience Enhancement
initiatives.summary: SJP elevated Cyber, Information Security and Operational Resilience to material risks in 2025 due to increased threat landscape and internal organisational change. The company enhanced its cyber security framework, conducted exercises, and developed playbooks and expert advice capabilities.

evidence.title: Cyber Security and Operational Resilience Enhancement
evidence.summary: SJP elevated Cyber, Information Security and Operational Resilience to material risks in 2025 due to increased threat landscape and internal organisational change. The company enhanced its cyber security framework, conducted exercises, and developed playbooks and expert advice capabilities.
evidence.quote: Cyber, Information Security and Operational Resilience risks have all increased in 2025 and are now viewed as material risks across the SJP Group. This is due to the significant increase in the threat landscape and the volume of internal organisational change that SJP has experienced... The Committee has noted the value of playbooks and expert advice in tackling cyber security whilst also recognising the need to continually evolve its approach in this area to keep abreast of developments.

initiatives.name: External Auditor Transition
initiatives.summary: Following a competitive tender process in 2025, Forvis Mazars were selected as the preferred audit firm to replace PwC in 2027. The selection follows regulatory requirements to change audit firms after PwC's appointment since 2009.

evidence.title: New External Auditor Selected Following Tender Process
evidence.summary: Following a competitive tender process in 2025, Forvis Mazars were selected as the preferred audit firm to replace PwC in 2027. The selection follows regulatory requirements to change audit firms after PwC's appointment since 2009.
evidence.quote: As a result of the process, I am pleased to share that Forvis Mazars were selected as the preferred audit firm to replace PwC in 2027, subject to Shareholder approval at the 2027 AGM.

initiatives.name: Climate Targets and Carbon Reduction
initiatives.summary: SJP set new interim climate targets including reducing combined Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 65% by 2030 and investment carbon intensity by 50% by 2030. The company achieved a 37.5% reduction in investment carbon intensity since 2019, exceeding its 2025 target.

evidence.title: New Climate Targets and Carbon Reduction
evidence.summary: SJP set new interim climate targets including reducing combined Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 65% by 2030 and investment carbon intensity by 50% by 2030. The company achieved a 37.5% reduction in investment carbon intensity since 2019, exceeding its 2025 target.
evidence.quote: We aim to reduce our combined Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 65% by 2030 (baseline year: 2023) and the carbon intensity of our investments by 50% by 2030 (baseline year: 2019). The weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of our investments has reduced by 37.5% since 2019, as at 31 December 2025.
